discovery: Transiting exoplanets and the first measurement of an exoplanet atmosphere

nominees.name: David Charbonneau
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University / Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

motivation: In 1999-2000 Charbonneau and Henry independently observed HD 209458b passing in front of its star, the first transit of a planet outside the Solar System. The measurement gave the planet's radius and, with radial velocities, its true mass and density, which established that hot Jupiters are gas giants. Seager predicted that starlight filtered through a transiting planet's limb would carry atmospheric absorption features. In 2002 Charbonneau and collaborators detected sodium in HD 209458b's atmosphere with the Hubble Space Telescope, the first measurement of an exoplanet atmosphere. Transit photometry and transmission spectroscopy are now the basis of Kepler, TESS and JWST. They have turned thousands of distant worlds into physical systems whose structure, composition and climate can be measured. Like the best planetary exploration, this work made an invisible environment measurable through careful, indirect observation, and it created a new branch of physics.
